 Penguins forward Ben Kindel hospitalized in Utah
Team says Kindel is ‘conscious, alert and in stable condition’
 By Seth Rorabaugh 1 Min Read 
 • Oct. 20, 2026 
 | 26 seconds ago 
-->
 Go Ad-Free today 
 Penguins forward Ben Kindel was a first-round selection (No. 11 overall) in the 2025 NHL Draft. (AP) 
 Pittsburgh Penguins forward Ben Kindel was hospitalized Tuesday in Salt Lake City after experiencing what was termed a “medical episode” according to a statement issued by the team.
 The nature or severity of Kindel’s ailment was not disclosed.
 The Penguins were traveling home Tuesday following a 5-4 loss to the Utah Mammoth on Monday evening. Per the statement, the team’s plane returned to Salt Lake City International Airport shortly after takeoff and team physician Dr. Dharmesh Vyas and other team medical staffers onboard attended to Kindel.
 Kindel was transferred to the University of Utah Hospital for further evaluation. According to the statement, Kindel is “conscious, alert and in stable condition.”
 No further details as to Kindel’s status or whether the team returned to Pittsburgh were provided.
 Kindel, 19, is in his second NHL season. A first-round draft pick (No. 11 overall) in 2025, Kindel has appeared in nine games this season and has scored four points (two goals, two assists) while averaging 17:19 of ice time per contest, primarily as the team’s third-line center.
 A statement from the Pittsburgh Penguins https://t.co/fyFReh2BWL
